newsitem.title: INDIA: Gujral sees no dramatic result from Pakistan talks.
newsitem.headline: Gujral sees no dramatic result from Pakistan talks.

text.p: Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said he does not expect dramatic results from diplomatic talks with Pakistan scheduled for later this week, the Asian Age newspaper reported on Monday.
"...I do not expect dramatic results. Both of us should not expect this," Gujral was quoted as saying.
"The meeting by itself is a process, and after all, these things have happened for three (or) four decades, it takes time to unlock them also," he said.
Talks between the two countries' foreign secretaries are scheduled to begin in New Delhi on Friday. Negotiations have been stalled since January 1994.
"I welcome the situation in which these talks are taking place, and we are approaching it in a very constructive, positive kind of way," Gujral said.
Cooperation in areas of trade, travel and culture can strengthen bilateral ties between the two South Asian neighbours, he added.
"There are several things that can be done by agreements. Travel, trade, people to people relations, culture, several things can be done and which should be done," Gujral said.
Last week, India relaxed visa restrictions for Pakistani businessmen and journalists, and said Pakistani tourist groups would be allowed to visit India.
Pakistan in a goodwill gesture released 38 Indian children on Sunday held for about three years after being detained when Indian fishing boats were seized.
The children were among more than 100 people detained aboard Indian fishing boats caught in Pakistani waters in recent years.
Gujral said he had told the Indian parliament that two basic issues -- "secular unity" and "sovereignty" of India were "not negotiable" in the talks with Pakistan.
Gujral is scheduled to meet Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan at a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement in April in New Delhi.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is due to meet his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, on the sidelines of a regional summit in the Maldives in May.
